audit_findings.title: Growth may require capital spending excluded from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 capital expenditures $363.5m versus depreciation and amortization $251.8m; $111.7m difference equals 16.2% of the $689.4m OE anchor; growth-capex portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Required manufacturing, equipment and working-capital reinvestment would reduce forecast OE supporting the 3% and 6% growth cases.
audit_findings.evidence: As demand grows for our products, we will continue to expand global operations to meet demand through investments in manufacturing and operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates substantial continuing investment requirements, but it does not establish whether the valuation classified and deducted all capital required for growth. The observable capex-to-depreciation difference is large enough relative to the anchor that an omitted recurring reinvestment charge could materially reduce the explicit-period and terminal cash flows. This is a potentially material classification error, not a demonstrated dollar-for-dollar omission.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2025 capex and working-capital investment between maintenance and expansion categories, map each growth scenario to required reinvestment using operational capacity plans, and rerun all scenarios deducting the supported amounts.

audit_findings.title: Unreserved litigation claims may sit ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: Uninsured damages, settlements and incremental defense costs would reduce future OE or require a direct deduction in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Due to uncertainty surrounding the securities class action litigation, the derivative actions, and the G6 and G7 Class Action Litigation we are unable to reasonably estimate the ultimate outcome of any of the litigation matters at this time.
audit_findings.explanation: The pending securities, derivative and product class actions are demonstrated, and both the 10-K and June 2026 10-Q state that their outcomes cannot be reasonably estimated. The record does not demonstrate an omitted probable liability or provide a loss range, so this is an unresolved possibility rather than an established valuation error. It could affect common equity, but materiality cannot be determined.
audit_findings.action: Obtain current case-status assessments, accrued contingencies, reasonably possible loss ranges, insurance limits and exclusions, defense-cost forecasts and settlement demands; rerun the bridge for any expected uninsured outflow.

audit_findings.title: Convertible-note shares and the earnings numerator describe different claims
audit_findings.magnitude: 7.696375m conversion shares, 1.98% of the 388.75714m denominator; removing those shares while retaining after-interest OE raises base value from $30.28 to approximately $30.89 per share; filed 2026 first-half after-tax interest add-back was $3.3m
audit_findings.mechanism: The denominator assumes conversion dilution while OE retains the interest expense associated with the debt claim.
audit_findings.evidence: The 2028 Notes may be settled upon conversion in cash, stock, or a combination thereof, solely at our discretion.
audit_findings.explanation: The hybrid claim construction is demonstrated, but its scale does not change the conclusion. On the debt-consistent treatment, eliminating 7.696375m shares increases base value by about $0.61 per share, and the $87.90 market price remains about 185% above the adjusted $30.89 base value. An equity-consistent treatment would also remove related after-tax interest, but the filed first-half amount is small relative to the $689.4m anchor.
audit_findings.action: Select either debt settlement with no conversion shares and retained interest or stock settlement with conversion shares and removal of related after-tax interest, then rerun per-share values and reflect the capped-call terms consistently.

audit_findings.title: The explicit 2028 reimbursement reduction may require an OE step-down
audit_findings.mechanism: Lower Medicare reimbursement beginning in 2028 could reduce revenue, margins and OE during the explicit forecast and flow into terminal earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result, we expect that Medicare reimbursement for our CGM systems will decrease beginning in 2028.
audit_findings.explanation: The expected reimbursement decrease is explicitly disclosed, but it is forward-looking and the filing supplies neither Medicare-exposed revenue nor the expected price reduction. Nonnegative net growth is not itself proof of omission because volume growth or cost savings could offset lower reimbursement. The issue nevertheless requires monitoring because it starts inside the forecast period and could affect the terminal base.
audit_findings.action: Quantify Medicare-exposed units and revenue, competitive-bid pricing, distributor pass-through, volume response and cost offsets when bid information becomes available, then rerun each scenario with an explicit 2028 adjustment.

audit_findings.title: The single-year anchor is sensitive to pharmacy-rebate estimation
audit_findings.magnitude: $50.1m revenue change for each one-percentage-point change in estimated products subject to rebate, equal to 1.1% of FY2025 revenue and 7.3% of the $689.4m OE anchor before considering costs and taxes
audit_findings.mechanism: A rebate true-up changes FY2025 revenue and OE, and the single-year anchor propagates that change through every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: An increase or decrease of 1% in our estimate of products sold subject to rebate during 2025, holding all other assumptions constant, would increase or decrease revenue by approximately $50.1 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The estimate sensitivity is demonstrated, but no actual FY2025 misstatement or subsequent material true-up is identified. The direction could increase or decrease value, and a revenue sensitivity cannot be translated into OE without the settlement difference, margin and tax effects. Its materiality therefore remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the FY2025 rebate accrual to 2026 settlements and true-ups, eligibility and channel-inventory data; normalize the anchor for any identified prior-period adjustment and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: A finite and conditional tax holiday may be embedded in terminal earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 Malaysia foreign-rate differential benefit $14.8m, equal to 2.1% of the $689.4m OE anchor; recurring benefit, retroactive catch-up and post-expiry tax cost unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The tax holiday increases current OE, while carrying the benefited tax rate beyond the conditional holiday would overstate explicit or terminal OE.
audit_findings.evidence: We have been granted a tax incentive by the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA) in Malaysia, which provides for a 0% tax holiday of up to 15 years based on our ability to meet certain conditions.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the holiday is conditional, lasts no more than 15 years and was applied retroactively to January 1, 2024. The current filed benefit is modest relative to the anchor, but the record does not separate the catch-up from recurring savings or quantify Malaysian taxable income when the holiday expires. Consequently, present scale does not establish terminal materiality.
audit_findings.action: Separate the 2024 catch-up from recurring FY2025 savings, document the holiday commencement and maximum expiry dates and compliance conditions, forecast Malaysian taxable income, and rerun the DCF using the post-holiday tax rate when applicable.
